reports.text:
Indication: right flank pain and gross hematuria; sickle cell disease.
Right kidney measures within normal limits for length. Left kidney normal in size. Normal cortical echogenicity bilaterally. No hydronephrosis. No renal calculi. No perinephric collection. Bladder partially distended, unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Normal-sized kidneys without hydronephrosis or stones.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary, hematology
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, Hematology inpatient service. Admitted 01/09/2026, discharged 01/16/2026.

Reason for admission: acute vaso-occlusive pain crisis.

History: 23-year-old man with HbSS, prior acute chest syndrome as a teenager, renal papillary necrosis of the left kidney in May 2025, and malignant hyperthermia susceptibility after a reaction during cholecystectomy in 2024. Admitted with a typical pain crisis managed with IV fluids and IV analgesia.

Course: On hospital day 3 he developed new right flank pain with visibly bloody urine. He denied trauma, known kidney stones or urinary infections; his renal function has been stable at baseline. Exam: right costovertebral angle tenderness, afebrile, no suprapubic tenderness. Urinalysis: gross hematuria with rare white cells, no casts. Hematocrit 22% on admission, 10% on day 3. Renal ultrasound: normal-sized kidneys, no hydronephrosis, no stones. Impression: recurrent renal papillary necrosis, now right-sided. He received 4 units of packed red cells over two days. Hematuria cleared over the following days and pain settled. Hematocrit 24% on the morning of discharge.

Discharge diagnoses: HbSS with vaso-occlusive crisis; renal papillary necrosis, right; acute fall in hematocrit, transfused.
Discharge medications: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, albuterol HFA as needed. No NSAIDs.
Allergies: NKDA. MH susceptible: avoid volatile anesthetics and succinylcholine.
Family history: father and mother with sickle cell trait; maternal uncle with suspected malignant hyperthermia under anesthesia; paternal grandmother with asthma.
Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol, college student working part-time in retail.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 to 2 weeks with CBC; hematology clinic in 4 to 6 weeks.

documents.title: Family call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's mother called (verbal consent on file from pt to speak with her). Curtis has been in the hospital since Friday with a sickle cell pain crisis and then had blood in his urine again, other side this time; he needed blood transfusions. Expected home in a few days. Asked her to have him book a follow-up with us within 1-2 weeks of discharge. Will request records.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: after hospitalization
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospitalized 1/9-1/16 for a sickle pain crisis. No discharge summary yet; history from Curtis, his discharge paperwork and his mother's call.
Per patient: pain crisis treated with IV meds; on the third day his right side started hurting and his urine went red. Told it was the kidney papilla problem again, other kidney. His blood count dropped a lot and he got several units of blood. Home since Friday. Urine has looked normal for 4 or 5 days. Pain gone. Tired but improving, back in class Monday. Taking hydroxyurea and folic acid; no ibuprofen.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Mild icterus, conjunctivae a little pale. Heart RRR, flow murmur. Lungs clear. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft.
CBC today: Hgb 8.1, Hct 24.3, essentially back near his usual.

A/P
1. Vaso-occlusive crisis, resolved.
2. Renal papillary necrosis, now right side as well as left last May. Hydration, NSAID avoidance reinforced.
3. Post-transfusion anemia check: Hct 24.3, acceptable. Copy to hematology; he sees them next month.
4. Records request for discharge summary.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hospital medical records says first request from 1/22 was not received. Re-faxed request with signed release for 1/9-1/16 admission.

documents.title: Discharge summary received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Discharge summary for January admission received. Scanned and sent to PCP.

documents.title: Hematology clinic letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Adult Sickle Cell Program. Seen 02/24/2026.

Dear colleague,
Curtis is seen after his January admission for a vaso-occlusive crisis complicated by right-sided renal papillary necrosis and a marked fall in hematocrit requiring transfusion. He has recovered well, with no hematuria or pain since discharge. We again discussed taking hydroxyurea every day rather than intermittently; he will try. Counts today near his steady state.

Plan: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily and folic acid 1 mg daily, continued. Avoid NSAIDs. Hydration. CBC and retic every 3 months. Return in 4 to 5 months.
Allergies: NKDA. MH susceptible.

Kind regards,
Hematology attending

documents.title: Folic acid refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request for folic acid 1 mg. Hematology prescription ran out of refills and pt asked them to send to us. Okayed by PCP, 90 days with 3 refills.

documents.title: form for summer job
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, work needs a form saying I can do stockroom shifts this summer. Can you fill it out? Also is it ok for me to do lifting with the sickle cell

documents.title: RE: form for summer job
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Curtis, form is done and in your portal documents. Lifting is fine. The main things with your sickle cell are staying very well hydrated, taking breaks in the heat, and avoiding getting overheated or chilled. Also a good reminder you're due for your physical; please book for early August.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical. Summer break from school, picking up extra shifts at the store.
Since January: no further admissions, no flank pain, no red urine. Saw hematology in February and again in July (July note not received; he says no changes). Trying to take hydroxyurea daily now, admits he still misses some days. Folic acid daily. Albuterol only once or twice since spring.
Meds: hydroxyurea 1000 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, albuterol HFA prn. NKDA; MH-susceptible alert. Wears the alert bracelet.
Social: never smoker, drinks rarely.
ROS: negative.

Exam: vitals as charted. Mild scleral icterus as always. Heart with his usual soft systolic murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No CVA tenderness. No leg ulcers. Normal gait and strength.

A/P
- HbSS on hydroxyurea; recurrent papillary necrosis (L 5/2025, R 1/2026): CBC, retic, CMP, UA today. Hydration at work, no NSAIDs.
- MH susceptibility: alert in chart, reviewed.
- Mild intermittent asthma: controlled.
- Prevention: flu and COVID this fall, either here or with hematology. PHQ-2 0.
- Records request to hematology for July note.
Follow up in a year or as needed.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Curtis, your hemoglobin and retic are back at your usual levels, kidney function is normal, and the urine shows no blood. Copies sent to hematology.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to hematology clinic for July 2026 visit note.

documents.title: Albuterol refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request albuterol HFA. Last fill February. Approved, 1 inhaler with 1 refill.
